# Path Violation Census

Scope: `langgraph_engine/`, `hooks/`, `scripts/`, `src/` (live scope only, `.venv/` excluded).
Method: full `ast` parse of all 335 live-scope `.py` files plus line-level regex on the same file set
(no syntax errors encountered; 0 files skipped).

## Totals

| Section | Count |
|---|---|
| (a) home-dir Claude path references (`~/.claude/...`, `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\...`) | **116** |
| (b) absolute path literals (`C:\...`, `/Users/...`) | **0** |
| (c) text-mode `open()` without explicit `encoding=` | **19** |

Orchestrator baseline for (c) was 12. **This census corrects it to 19** — see the full list below;
all 19 are genuine text-mode calls with no binary indicator (no `"rb"`/`"wb"` literal, no `mode=` kwarg
containing `b`), so none qualify for the binary-mode exemption.

---

## (a) Home-dir Claude path references — 116 occurrences, 48 files

Split by whether the reference is a live default/assignment (needs `path_resolver.py`) vs. a
comment/docstring/CLI-help string (informational; lower priority but still drifts from the
single-source-of-truth path convention):

- **Code-level (default parameter, `os.environ.get` default, or assignment) — 13 occurrences** — these are the ones that actually construct a runtime path and should route through `path_resolver.py`.
- **Comment/docstring/CLI-help text — 103 occurrences** — mostly in `langgraph_engine/error_messages.py` (10, user-facing troubleshooting hints like `ls ~/.claude/skills/`) and CLI `--help` strings in `context_sync/architecture/*.py`. These do not execute as paths but still hardcode the convention outside `path_resolver.py` and will silently go stale if the layout changes.

### Code-level occurrences (fix candidates)

these files should reference `path_resolver.py`'s helper names in the comment text (not the raw
`~/.claude/...` string) so the comment cannot drift independently of the code.

## (b) Absolute path literals — 0 occurrences

Scanned for both `'C:\...'`/`"C:\..."` (Windows drive-letter literal) and `'/Users/...'`/`"/Users/..."`
(macOS/Linux home literal) as quoted string constants across all 335 live-scope files. **None found.**
This is a positive finding: it corroborates CLAUDE.md's own rule ("Always use path_resolver.py for
cross-platform paths") — the codebase appears to actually follow it for drive-letter/home-literal
paths, even though it does not consistently follow it for `~/.claude/` shorthand (see section (a)).

Caveat: this regex only catches *quoted string constants*. It cannot catch an absolute path built by
runtime string concatenation or passed in via an environment variable/CLI argument. No occurrence of
that pattern was specifically searched for in this pass; treat "0" as "0 literal occurrences," not
"proof no absolute path ever appears at runtime."

Proposed fix (uniform across all 19): add `encoding="utf-8"` to every call, per CLAUDE.md's own
Windows-platform rule ("use UTF-8 encoding, ASCII-only in Python files (cp1252 safe)"). Each of
these is a plain `with open(path) as f:` or `with open(path, "w") as f:` reading/writing JSON,
config, or markdown — none has a documented reason to rely on the platform default codepage, so
`encoding="utf-8"` is a safe drop-in fix in all 19 cases.
